text:
Sam K: quick thought — i'm drafting an RFC about a dependency-injection shim for hosting modes (hosted/dedicated/private). want to capture tradeoffs before i write the formal doc. TL;DR: small runtime shim that injects mode-specific wiring vs bigger adapter layer that translates entire config. what do folks think?
Anya P: curious — what problems are we trying to solve that current adapters don't?
Sam K: good q. current pain: duplicated wiring for auth/secrets/telemetry across adapters, different fallback behavior for model variants, and tests that only work in one mode. goal is one concise surface for business logic + small pluggable bits per mode.
Lee M: +1 to reducing duplication. tradeoff is complexity at runtime. if shim is too magical we lose observability and it becomes hard to debug mode-specific bugs.
Darius: i worry about ownership — who owns the shim code? infra or runtime? also secrets handling differs a lot between hosted and private (KMS vs customer HSM).
Sam K: thinking: shim lives in runtime repo, but has an explicit "mode provider" interface implemented by each hosting pack (hosted provider, dedicated provider, private provider). runtime exposes hooks for: auth, secret-resolve, route-policy, telemetry-fanout.
Anya P: can we keep the provider impls tiny? like just a metadata map + callbacks, not full-on adapters. example: provider = { resolveSecret(key) => promise, telemetrySink(ctx) => sinkId }
Lee M: yep, keep impls surface minimal. also require providers to declare capabilities (canProxyKVCache, supportsAbort, supportsBurst) so runtime can gate features.
Sam K: exactly. capability manifest seems necessary. otherwise we get weird fallbacks at runtime. manifest could be simple JSON. e.g.:
```json
{"capabilities": ["kvcache","burst","kms-hsm"], "priority": 100}
```
Anya P: two more concerns: 1) config drift when manifests evolve, 2) rollout of new provider impls — need compatibility rules.
Darius: for drift i propose a strict schema + runtime reject on unknown required fields. rollouts: side-by-side registration with versioned provider ids, and canary route mapping.
Lee M: what about testability? i'd like a test harness to swap a fake provider that simulates latency, auth failures, secret unwrap errors. keeps unit tests deterministic.
Sam K: agree. runtime should expose a test provider registry and a small simulator lib. tests can assert that provider capability gating works (e.g., if provider lacks kvcache, cache calls return NOP but metric emitted).
Anya P: security note: provider interface must not leak raw encrypted blobs to runtime. provider should do unwrap locally for private mode, and return plaintext token only if allowed by policy. otherwise runtime can call provider.signaling only.
Darius: +1. also add an audit hook so private deployments can opt-in to audit events for secret access. logged in customer-controlled sink.
Sam K: okay next: runtime fallback policy. when a provider signals "unavailable" do we: a) fallback to a cheaper hosted provider variant b) queue request until provider recovers c) fail fast. i think make policy pluggable per route.
Lee M: pluggable per-route sounds right. defaults: hosted -> fast-fail to fallback variant; private -> fail-fast and bubble error. dedicated -> try burst fallback if configured.
Anya P: implementation detail: keep fallback decisions in a small policy DSL, not code. e.g.,
```yaml
route: /generate
fallbacks:
  - provider: hosted-fallback
    when: provider.unavailable and latency<100ms
  - action: fail
```
Darius: love DSL idea. enables product to change policies without shipping runtime. need validation server-side though.
Sam K: last bit: observability. shim must emit token-level latency, provider selection reasons, and capability-based metrics. also trace spans that include provider id and version.
infra-bot: deploy-checker: note — any runtime change touching secret resolution needs security review. tag: sec-review-required.
Sam K: noted. next steps: i'll draft the RFC with: provider interface spec, capability manifest schema, policy DSL sketch, test harness plan, and rollout playbook. please ping me if you want specific examples included.
Anya P: please include a small example of provider impl for on-prem HSM and a hosted minimal provider. real code snippet would help.
Lee M: i'll take the test harness section and add negative test cases.
Darius: i'll add security constraints and audit hook requirements.
Sam K: awesome — thanks team. closing for now, will post RFC link later. :thumbsup:
